_marks: **weight** · *motion* · !!impact!! — rendered by the surface; plain text everywhere else

decks.name: The System
decks.description: How Bot Army thinks: the rules, the design lens, and the scars behind them.

cards.front: Why does **every** bot change bump the version — even a comment?
cards.back: The version bump **is** the release signal. No bump → no GitHub release → nothing for `make deploy-bot` to deploy. And a `@moduledoc` is compiled into the BEAM, so "only a comment" still changes the release.
cards.hook: The version number is the *flag on the mast*. No new flag, and the fleet **doesn't know** the ship changed. !!No bump, no ship.!!

cards.front: Why do bots default to port **4223**, not 4222?
cards.back: Fail-safe. 4223 is the idle dev broker. A misconfigured bot lands there and runs harmlessly instead of posting bad data to production (4222). Every real deployment pins its port explicitly.
cards.hook: A cadet who forgets their orders reports to the *training sim*, not the **front line**. Notice how 4223 already feels like the *safe* number.

cards.front: A deploy printed green. Is the new version running?
cards.back: Not proven. Salt has exited 0 over `Failed: 1`; publish has printed success without requesting a deploy. Proof is the version the service **answers with** — curl its `/health`.
cards.hook: The bridge officer says *"hit confirmed"*. The captain asks: **"Show me the wreckage."** !!A green light is a claim, not a kill.!!

cards.front: What is the **Makefile** in a bot repo?
cards.back: The contract. Every operation — test, push, publish, deploy, logs — is a `make` target with its checks built in. If you're typing a sequence of three commands, it should be a target.
cards.hook: The Makefile is the *ship's manual*. You don't improvise the reactor startup — you **follow the checklist**, and the checklist remembers what you forget.

cards.back: A dotted name a message is sent to, like `terrain.tip.today` — domain, then noun, then verb. Request/reply subjects answer; event subjects just announce.
cards.hook: A subject is a *radio channel*. Tune to **terrain.tip.today** and someone *answers*. Tune to an event channel and you just **hear the news**.

cards.front: Design lens rule #1: what beats a dashboard?
cards.back: **One card.** The single next action, already broken down to a small first step. A 19-item list is where ADHD goes to feel shame.
cards.hook: Don't hand the captain *the whole star chart*. Hand her **one heading**. !!One card.!!

cards.front: How does the system talk about a task that's gone stale?
cards.back: It asks "still true?" — never accuses. No broken-streak guilt, no red overdue badges, no backlog-as-indictment.
cards.hook: The ship's AI doesn't say *"you failed"*. It says **"still true?"** — and you *notice how much lighter* that is to answer.

cards.front: 30009 vs 30014 — which page may show **rows** like `AAPL 10 @ 150`?
cards.back: Only 30014. 30009 has no door, so it shows counts and health. A row that names a person, account, body or amount goes behind a door. **The door decides the row.**
cards.hook: The *hangar* is open to anyone walking by — so it shows **how many ships**. The *captain's cabin* has a lock — so it shows **whose**.

cards.back: In ripgrep, `-r` is **--replace**, not recursive. `-rn` replaces every match with the letter `n` — the output looks plausible and is wrong. Use `rg -n` (ripgrep is already recursive).
cards.hook: Fourteen times the crew fired `-rn` and the scanner *quietly painted every target as "n"*. !!-r means replace.!! You'll **feel** your fingers stop before typing it.

cards.back: `{:ok, pid}` — not `:ok`. Two bots matched `:ok = Registry.register(...)` and crash-looped in production. (`Connection.subscribe/1` *does* return `:ok` — they look alike and aren't.)
cards.hook: Two calls in matching uniforms. One salutes **:ok**. The other hands you a *tuple*. Mistake them and the ship !!crash-loops!!.

cards.front: A press would send a value. Where must the value come from?
cards.back: From **her** press — never from a default the card opened on. Empty choice, disabled button until every fact is chosen, and a refusal in plain words. A card once filed a workout she never described.
cards.hook: The form never *fills itself in and salutes*. **Her** hand sets the dial. Then the ship moves.

cards.front: A press can't be undone. Lock it away?
cards.back: No — **build the undo.** Removal marks the row (`deleted_at`) and restore clears the mark, so the same card comes back with its history. Locking a door to cover a missing undo reads as distrust.
cards.hook: Don't *weld the airlock shut*. Install the **recall button**. !!Build the undo.!!

decks.name: Kubernetes
decks.description: The cluster under the bot army, one concept at a time.

cards.back: One or more containers sharing one network address and storage. The smallest thing Kubernetes schedules.
cards.hook: A *pea pod*: the peas **ride together**, share one shell, and get *thrown out together*.

cards.back: It's the agent on every node: it starts the pods assigned to that node and keeps watching them.
cards.hook: The control plane is the *admiral*. The kubelet is the **deck officer on each ship** who makes the orders *actually happen*.

cards.front: Deployment vs Pod — which do you create?
cards.back: A **Deployment**. It declares how many copies of a pod should exist and replaces them when they die. Bare pods are rare.
cards.hook: You don't order one marine. You order **a squad of three** — and when one falls, *a replacement drops in*.

cards.back: You declare what should exist; controllers keep moving reality toward it in a loop.
cards.hook: You say *what* you want. The control loop **nags reality** until it agrees. Very Skippy. Very *annoying*. !!Very reliable.!!

cards.back: A Service exposed on the same high port (30000–32767) on every node. Grafana is on **30091**, Prometheus on **30090**.
cards.hook: Every node has the *same numbered door* on its hull. Knock on **30091** and *Grafana* answers.

cards.back: Tunnels a local port into a pod or service. It's how Postgres reaches your Mac on **35432**.
cards.hook: A *wormhole*, one port wide: dial **35432** at home and you *come out* inside the cluster.

cards.back: A named partition inside a cluster that groups resources and scopes their names and access.
cards.hook: One hull, **different compartments** — engineering, medbay, the brig — with *hatches between them*.

cards.back: The container keeps exiting and Kubernetes waits longer between restarts. Read the last life's logs: `kubectl logs <pod> --previous`.
cards.hook: It *falls*, gets up, *falls*, and the medic waits longer each time. The **previous** life's logs tell you !!why it fell!!.

decks.name: Trading
decks.description: The words the strategy loop thinks in.

cards.back: Relative Strength Index, 0–100: recent gains vs losses, usually over 14 bars. Above 70 is often called overbought, below 30 oversold.
cards.hook: A *tachometer* for price. Past **70** the engine is *redlining*. Under **30** it's barely idling.

cards.back: When a fast average (say 20-bar) crosses the slow one (say 50-bar). Crossing above suggests momentum turning up; below, turning down.
cards.hook: Two ships on one heading. When the *fast* one **overtakes** the slow one, !!the fleet is turning!!.

cards.front: What is **ATR**, and why does the loop use it?
cards.back: Average True Range — the typical size of one bar's move. Stops are set a multiple away (e.g. 2× ATR) so normal noise doesn't hit them.
cards.hook: ATR is **the size of the waves**. Anchor *past* the usual wave, or ordinary chop knocks you overboard.

cards.front: An option's premium says **2.13**. What does one contract cost?
cards.back: **$213.** Premiums are quoted per share and one contract is 100 shares.
cards.hook: The tag says **2.13**; the *box holds 100*. The system once forgot the box and every number came out !!100× too big!!.

cards.back: An order filled by the simulator, not a real market. No money moves. 30014 says "paper" so "filled" doesn't pretend otherwise.
cards.hook: A *training round*. The trigger pulls, the target drops, and **nobody gets hurt**.

cards.front: What is the **$25,000** goal on the trading board?
cards.back: The Pattern Day Trader threshold: in a margin account, 4+ day trades in 5 business days requires $25,000 in equity.
cards.hook: A gate at **$25,000**. Below it, *four quick round trips* in a week and !!the gate slams!!.

cards.back: Limit: only at your price or better, and it may not fill. Market: fills now at whatever the price is.
cards.hook: Limit is a *sniper* — **only at this range**. Market is a *shotgun* — **now**, wherever it lands.

cards.front: On most days the loop answers `:wait`. Is that a failure?
cards.back: No. Being early is the same as being wrong. Waiting is a decision the loop records, not an absence of one.
cards.hook: The best captains **hold fire** until the range is right. *Wait* is an order too.

decks.name: Elixir
decks.description: The language the bots are written in.

cards.back: It **matches**, it doesn't assign. `{:ok, x} = result` succeeds only if the shapes line up, binding `x` on the way.
cards.hook: `=` is a *docking clamp*: it only **locks on** when the shapes fit. Wrong shape — !!MatchError!!.

cards.back: Passes the value on its left as the **first argument** of the call on its right.
cards.hook: A *conveyor belt*: the result **rides** to the next station and lands in *slot one*.

cards.front: What do `{:ok, value}` and `{:error, reason}` mean?
cards.back: The convention for a call that can fail: success carries the value, failure carries why. Callers match on the tag.
cards.hook: Every mission report starts with **one word**: *ok* or *error*. Read the word first, then the cargo.

cards.back: A process that holds state and answers messages — `call` (wait for a reply) and `cast` (fire and forget). Every bot store is one.
cards.hook: A *crew member* with a clipboard. **Call** and she answers. **Cast** and she just *notes it down*.

cards.back: Don't wrap everything defensively. If a process hits a state it can't handle, let it die — its supervisor restarts it clean.
cards.hook: The redshirt goes down; the **supervisor** beams down a fresh one *with a clean memory*.

cards.back: Runs a chain of matches in order. The first one that doesn't match skips to the `else` clauses.
cards.hook: A *series of airlocks*. Each one **must cycle green** before the next opens. One red light and you're *in the else*.

cards.front: Can you change a map in place?
cards.back: No. Data is **immutable**. `Map.put/3` returns a new map; the old one is untouched.
cards.hook: You never *edit* the log. You write a **new entry**, and the old one *stays exactly as it was*.

cards.back: The module's docs chunk inside the `.beam` file — which is why a doc-only edit still changes the release and still needs a version bump.
cards.hook: Even the *ship's diary* is **welded into the hull**. Change a word and !!it's a new ship!!.

decks.name: Greek
decks.description: The alphabet first, then the words of a morning.

cards.back: Alpha — "a" as in *father*.
cards.hook: **α** is a *fish swimming left*. The fish says **"ahh"**.

cards.front: **β** — name and sound in modern Greek?
cards.back: Vita — "v" as in *victory*.
cards.hook: **β** stands *tall like a Viking* — **V**ita, **V**iking, **v**.

cards.back: Delta — a soft "th" as in *this*.
cards.hook: **δ** is a curl of breath — tongue *between the teeth*: **th**is.

cards.back: "r" (rho), lightly rolled. It looks like a p and isn't.
cards.hook: **ρ** wears a *p costume*. Pull the mask off: it's an !!R!!.

cards.back: "ee" as in *see* (ita). It looks like an n.
cards.hook: **η** is an *n with a long tail*, and the tail **squeaks "ee!"** as it drags.

cards.back: Καλημέρα — *ka-lee-MEH-ra*.
cards.hook: **Kali** (good) + **mera** (day). Say it to the mirror *tomorrow* and notice it's **already there**.

cards.back: **Yes.** Pronounced "neh".
cards.hook: It *sounds* like "nay" and means !!YES!!. The language is **trolling you**. Remember the troll.

cards.back: Ευχαριστώ — *ef-ha-ree-STO*.
cards.hook: **Eucharist** — a *giving of thanks*. Same root. **ef-ha-ree-STO**, stress at the end like a *bow*.
